a01.text: An accounts-payable controls lead at a federal contractor
gets an email: new bank details,
eight days before $1.28 million in payments.
Policy says call back on a number that did not come from
the letter. In practice that number takes four systems to
find, so people call the one on the letter.
Probity reads the letter with NVIDIA Nemotron,
then discovers the vendor's real corporate family across
USAspending, SEC EDGAR and our own vendor master through
Zetaris, which joins them in one semantic layer.
The new address is real, but it belongs to a different
Booz Allen company that has never billed us.
Decision: hold, with a call-back number from SEC records.
Then, unasked, it checks the rest of Friday's run.
Every registry fact is live public data.

a02.text: Four agents, each with its own authority.
The Letter Reader reads the letter twice,
in two independent Nemotron Ultra calls;
the readings must agree field by field.
The Registry Scout runs a floor of Zetaris checks,
and Nemotron Lightning adds what it misses.
The Examiner re-runs each new link's Zetaris query and
checks the rows. Code decides the verdict.

a03.text: This letter told the AI to approve it,
in hidden lines. Probity quotes them as evidence,
never obeys, and holds the payment.

a04.text: Here is the real run. The reader quotes the letter,
including the line asking us not to use the old number.
The Scout checks the vendor master and the registries
through Zetaris. The address matches nothing we know,
so the Examiner sends the Scout back.
A coverage rule walks Booz Allen's family,
forty-one entities, and keeps the one in New Jersey.
A naive check would pass this:
it is a real Booz Allen address.

never billed us. The Examiner re-runs that query before it
counts. Decision: hold. The call-back number comes from

a05.text: Same name, two companies. It refuses to guess,
and writes a call-back script for each.

a06.text: Memory across sessions. An impersonation confirmed in one
session is remembered by the World Model;
a later L3Harris request reuses that bank account,

a07.text: If Zetaris is down, it says so and never approves.

a08.text: Every registry and ledger fact in this decision came from
Zetaris, which joins our vendor master,
USAspending and SEC EDGAR in one semantic layer.
Each one traces back to its rows:
source system, table, query id and row hash,
and you can re-run it. The sweep runs Zetaris data-quality
rules. Every agent call goes through Meterless Nightshift
to a pinned Nemotron model, and the ledger shows which.

a09.text: For a company we have never paid,
Ultra approves the SEC link from cited rows,

a10.text: Not asked, but checked: five Zetaris rules sweep Friday's
run, down to two vendors sharing one bank account.
In all, three other payments fail controls;
the controller gets a hold list in dollars.

a11.text: What was known when: scrub the graph back to before the
run, and the New Jersey company is not in it yet.

a12.text: It never moves money. Built Grok-first:
Grok built the Zetaris data layer and the end-to-end
tests; Claude Code built the agents and the interface.
